sara_support: heads-up — ACME (tenant acme-inc) reports a big p95/p99 regression on /v1/generate since 09:28 UTC after the 09:15 deploy. p95 jumped from ~480ms to ~2.3s, p99 to ~4.2s. They see intermittent 502s. Their requests are mostly chat-style (context ~2.5k tokens).

devon_oncall: thanks. Any backend logs or OOM signals? Tenant ID and sample request size?

sara_support: tenant: acme-inc (tenant-983). Sample request: prompt ~2500 tokens, max_new_tokens=512, temperature=0.2. From host logs: repeated slab eviction & KV growth warnings around 09:26. Posting trimmed log:```
[09:26:13] runtime: kv_allocator: slab_usage=0.82, kv_entries=2.9M, growth_rate=+12%/5m
[09:26:14] runtime: gpu_mem_pressure: p95_alloc_latency=12ms, p99_alloc_latency=840ms
[09:26:15] runtime: OOM: failed to allocate 256MB for KV cache; triggered eviction cycle
[09:26:16] runtime: eviction: evicted 128MB, reclaimed 32MB (fragmentation high)
[09:26:17] nginx: upstream 10.2.1.45 timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
```

sara_support: Also saw a few lines like `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in worker stderr for the same host.

alex_runtime: looks like GPU KV growth + fragmentation causing slow alloc path and falling back to slow eviction. Two-pronged: (1) immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact, (2) longer-term allocator/compaction fixes.

alex_runtime: immediate suggestions: 1) temporarily route acme-inc to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint (e.g., rwd-3b-quantized). 2) apply tenant-level concurrency cap (max_concurrency=4) and lower batch size. 3) enable aggressive slab compaction/eviction for the affected pool: `SLA_ABS_THRESHOLD=0.65`, `KV_EVICT_MODE=aggressive` (quick and dirty). 4) if needed, drain and restart the hot worker after eviction to defragment.

marta_infra: adding infra notes — rolling a worker restart is low-risk if we drain first. I can pin acme-inc to a dedicated pool or move them to a different region for the next 30m. PR ready to change compaction frequency: https://git.internal/r/redwood/allocator/pulls/452 (patch increases compaction sweep to every 30s for high-heat pools).

devon_oncall: can you run these diagnostic commands on the host with the hotspot?`/usr/local/bin/runtime_ctl kv-stats --histogram --tenant tenant-983 > /tmp/acme-kv-hist.json` and `/usr/local/bin/runtime_ctl dump-alloc-map --short > /tmp/alloc-map.txt` — we need bucket distribution and free slab fragmentation.

alex_runtime: also capture p95/p99 per-gpu and per-tenant heatmap: `promql: sum by (tenant)(rate(gpu_kv_alloc_fail_total[5m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant))`.

sara_support: I applied a soft throttle (rate limit 30rpm) + set max_concurrency=4 for acme-inc; routed 15% of their traffic to rwd-3b-quantized. After those changes at 09:55 UTC p95 dropped to ~620ms, p99 to ~1.1s. Still above baseline but much better.

marta_infra: started compaction-sweep patch in canary pool at 10:02 UTC. Will monitor fragmentation metrics. If that continues to trend down we can promote.

devon_oncall: follow-ups for postmortem checklist: 1) link sample requests and full logs for affected hosts, 2) confirm allocator settings and config drift (SLA_ABS_THRESHOLD), 3) estimate memory leakage vs KV churn rate, 4) run replay on dev cluster with identical request mix to reproduce.

alex_runtime: long-term fixes we discussed: - reduce per-tenant KV retention for chat sessions older than 2k tokens, - implement background compaction that coalesces free slabs before eviction (less fragmentation), - guardrail on kv_entries growth with backpressure signals (reject/slow-path before OOM).

sara_support: ACME confirmed impact reduced; they're OK with temporary throttle while we stabilise. I'll keep them updated.

ops_bot: INCIDENT-4765432190 marked RESOLVED by sara_support at 10:12 UTC (auto-note: auto-ack from ops_bot).

sara_support: filing ticket for postmortem and owner assignment — assigning to alex_runtime and marta_infra. Will add repro artifacts and timelines. :white_check_mark:
